title: Rotate Image
prompt: You are given an `n x n` 2D matrix representing an image. Rotate the image by 90 degrees clockwise, in place. You must modify the matrix directly without allocating another 2D matrix.
hints: Rotating into a brand new n x n matrix and copying it back is O(n^2) time and space — can you eliminate the extra matrix?
A 90-degree clockwise rotation is exactly the same result as transposing the matrix (swap matrix[i][j] with matrix[j][i]) followed by reversing each row.
Both the transpose and the row-reversal can be done with simple swaps directly on the original matrix, needing no auxiliary storage.

solution.approach: A 90-degree clockwise rotation can be decomposed into two simpler in-place operations: first transpose the matrix (swap matrix[i][j] with matrix[j][i] for all i < j, flipping it across the main diagonal), then reverse each row. Transposing turns columns into rows, and reversing each row then flips left-to-right, which together produce exactly the clockwise rotation. Both steps only swap elements within the existing matrix, so no auxiliary matrix is ever allocated.
